minutes.headline: Board included nearly all FY27 warrant articles; TC Passios' safety issues leave the food pantry's future unresolved.
minutes.summary: The Select Board worked through most of the draft FY2027 annual town meeting warrant, voting to include (and in some cases recommend) dozens of articles covering capital cleanup items, union contract funding, an OPEB trust appropriation, a vacation-buyout liability reduction, and several bylaw changes, while holding off on the override placeholder, trust fund commission articles, a stormwater bylaw, and the Central Mass Mosquito Control article pending more information. The board also heard an extended, unresolved presentation from the Lunenburg Community Food Pantry about the deteriorating TC Passios building, where the food pantry currently operates, and closed a public hearing on opting out of mail-in early voting before entering executive session to discuss a collective bargaining agreement.

attendees.role: presenter, president of the Lunenburg Community Food Pantry

public_comment.topic: Urged the board to have the Municipal Building Design Committee take up TC Passios' town administrative functions (records storage, elections) and suggested charging the food pantry rent.
A board member (not a floor speaker) noted the board is continuing conversations about placing an override on the ballot for both school and town sides.

what_happened.line: The board voted to include most of the draft FY2027 town meeting warrant, including the Prop 2.5 override placeholder article, without recommending it.
It held off on the trust fund commission bylaw and legal-fees articles, a stormwater utility bylaw, and Central Mass Mosquito Control participation, pending legal review or more resident input.
An extended presentation on the deteriorating TC Passios building, where the food pantry operates, ended without a decision on relocation or the building's future.
The board closed a public hearing and voted unanimously to opt out of mail-in early voting for local elections this year.
The board entered executive session to discuss a collective bargaining agreement; that portion of the recording has no audio.

why_it_matters: Residents will see a Prop 2.5 override placeholder on the FY2027 warrant, though the board has not recommended it, so it will be a question voters take up at town meeting.
The food pantry's future home is unresolved: the board said it will not fund TC Passios roof or heating repairs without a broader plan for the building.
A handful of warrant articles -- a stormwater bylaw, mosquito control participation, and trust fund commission bylaws -- are still open and could return changed before town meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: On everything both records actually cover — the TC Passios/food pantry figures, the capital and trust-fund appropriations, the vacation buyout, the mosquito-control deferral, and the School Committee deficit numbers — the two agree closely, with only one clear caption-splitting error (the cemetery total) and two misheard names. The real gap is structural: our minutes have no entry at all for roughly seventeen routine warrant-article "include" votes, for the Public Employee Committee ratification vote, or for the Executive Session that preceded it, so a reader relying on ours alone would not know those votes happened.
